key_insight: Increasing Y content in BCFZY cathodes modestly improves proton transport under PCFC operating conditions, while low oxygen partial pressure is predicted to shift transport from hydroxyl to hydride species.
engineering_relevance: Cathode optimization should account for operating gas conditions rather than assume Y-doping gains measured under reducing conditions will transfer to PCFC air electrodes.
method: Use ab initio molecular dynamics to compare proton tracer diffusivity across three Y/Zr compositions.
Model hydration, oxidation, and hydride formation to estimate temperature-dependent proton concentrations.
Separate diffusivity and concentration contributions to proton conductivity.
evidence_signal: At 500 °C, replacing the Zr fraction in BCFZ with Y to form BCFY predicts increases of 1.7% in proton diffusivity, 3.8% in proton concentration, and 5.3% in proton conductivity under PCFC operating gas conditions.
watch_item: The predicted gains are modest and gas-dependent; experimental validation under representative cathode conditions is needed.
paper_title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O$_{3-δ}$ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells
